Schon seit Jahren leben unter Aufsicht einer (US-?!)Regierungsbehörde Aliens unter uns. Diese Behörden wird durch einen unorthodoxen Rookie verstärkt der direkt bei der Rettung der Erde unterstützen muss. Moderner Klassiker als klassisches Buddy-Movie, das sich durch schnelles Tempo, damals revolutionäre Effekte und großen Style-Willen auszeichnet. Ich bin kein Fan von Tommy Lee Jones und schon gar nicht von Will Smith, die Odd-Couple-Jokes sind also an mir verschwendet. Ebenso die schwarzen Anzüge, die doofen Sonnenbrillen und der ganze Retro-Futurismus-Klumpatsch. Am besten gefallen mir noch die Aliens, die sich als eher suspekte menschliche Charaktere tarnen und einige sehr witzige Dialogzeilen der Aliens. Den Kindern hat's gefallen, immerhin.

Driven by the eccentric nature it embraces, the film pushes beyond conventional boundaries, but ultimately never reaches its undeniable limits. It’s one of those classic movies that is considered iconic because it started something new or elevated a past project, still iconic isn’t equivalent to good, appreciative but never good. Well, still it has some good qualities that seems never to be conducted In an essential trajectory. I absolutely like the chemistry between Tommy Lee jones and will smith, it truly indicates it’s kind of mentor and master relationship, it simply showcases the passing of the torch, combining their unique personas to generate somewhat a hilarious dynamic. I know it undisputedly trying to speculate some goofy shit, but it never seems to excite me in nearly every scene. I personally think it shares some Scooby-Doo esque qualities, but explores them through a more mature lens that never dignifies its eccentric and exhilarating structure with undue seriousness. It definitely thrives with complete and utter priority with how sophisticated visual composition are. Sculpting with identity rather than unimaginative style, benefiting the restorative design it features. Immensely overrated. Never flourishing in succeeding to genuinely showcase it’s premise with care, and undoubtedly cringy in some respects that I found myself just wanting to close my eyes. 4.7/10

I finally watched Men in Black for the first time. Obviously I knew how culturally significant and iconic it became, but unfortunately I never watched it as a kid, and I think that probably would’ve changed my experience with it quite a bit. I can definitely see the appeal, especially as a kids’ movie. The whole concept of aliens secretly living among humans disguised as normal people is really creative, and combining that with two agents hunting down aliens, weird gadgets and goofy humor makes for a fun ’90s premise. The concept was probably more interesting to me than the actual story, though. The plot just never really caught me. It basically comes down to them chasing a big alien who’s looking for a galaxy hidden on a cat’s collar, and the whole thing felt pretty random and messy to me. There wasn’t really a storyline or mystery that made me particularly curious about what was going to happen next. There are some funny moments, and Will Smith does his usual charismatic Will Smith thing, but nothing about the characters or story really stood out to me. The effects are also pretty decent considering this came out in 1997, even if they’ve obviously aged. Overall, I can appreciate Men in Black for what it is and understand why a lot of people who grew up with it still love it. It’s a goofy, creative and very ‘90s sci-fi action comedy that probably would’ve worked much better for me as a kid. I’m glad I finally watched such a big pop-culture classic, but I don’t really feel the need to watch it again anytime soon.

Tommy Lee Jones and Will Smith Star in I would argue some of their most iconic roles as J and K in 1997's men in black A funny and fun movie over all that I feel could have went a bit deeper into the world building aspect. Albeit at a tight 90 minute run time everything you need in this movie is already here, it really just boils down to personal preference. Would have liked to get more interaction with aliens just living their daily lives. Special effects are the way to do it here, a mix of practical with CGI (and it's that good pre 2000's CGI) all of the set pieces are fun and interesting, and the movie definitely has something to say about ones duty to the human race in terms of keeping the peace. However in recent years, shady government agencies with little to no oversight that are a complete secret from the public at large is something I'm inherently distrustful of (I understand this movie was of the times). Loved will smiths growth here and how he went from brightly colored outfits to the classic black suit. The giant cockroach alien as well scared the fuck out of me as a kid now I watch it and I laugh because of the camp and charm of this movie. Mother fucker literally walks like Frankenstein which I think was the point. Tommy Lee jones plays a very reserved role here, mentor like figure with no time for jokes and a past barely mentioned (because who you were before doesn't matter). Shame he got vored at the end but hey at least he got out and at least he doesn't remember it. Need to watch the sequels next. Would watch again but this for sure is not my favorite movie. Still trying to figure out what didn't land with me.

неплохой фильм, но я почему-то ожидала от него немного большего. сама идея с секретной организацией, которая следит за инопланетянами и скрывает их существование от людей, прикольная, и за уиллом смитом было интересно наблюдать. особенно понравилось его знакомство с агентом кеем. еще отдельно хочу отметить костюмы уилла смита до того, как он вступил в эту корпорацию - вот они мне реально очень понравились. выглядел он в них просто пиздец как круто, особенно в сценах с полицейской работой. из запоминающегося еще всякие инопланетяне, жук и моменты с нейтрализатором памяти. некоторые сцены реально смешные, особенно когда показывают, насколько странным на самом деле является этот мир. но графика для нашего времени выглядит ну очень нереалистично. хотя я понимаю, что для 1997 года это, наверное, было вообще супер и зрители тогда наверняка офигевали от таких эффектов. сейчас просто некоторые пришельцы и эффекты выглядят настолько пластиково, что я больше хихикала, чем пугалась. в целом фильм прикольный, легкий и с хорошей атмосферой, но какого-то огромного вау-эффекта у меня не вызвал

Good fun. Obviously it's not super deep or challenging but for a family science fiction, this is a good time. Leave it to pre-9/11 Barry Sonnenfeld to make a proper action comedy that anyone can enjoy. Speaking of which, the twin towers are just... ever-present in this. I can't help but to chuckle at the thought of families needing to pause Men In Black to explain fucking 9/11 to their kids. Hysterical. Better to learn about it from a movie and loving parents than some twisted conspiracy nut on the playground. The amount of misinformation I was fed by peers while growing up is staggering. I digress. Will Smith and Tommy Lee Jones have real chemistry and they work very well independently as well. They're simply a great duo and the single best part of this film. Edgar Suit Bug is a close second though. I LOVE Vincent D'Onofrio (I definitely fucked up that spelling, sorry Vince) in this. The raw physicality and deterioration of Edgar is amazing. The makeup/costume people knocked it out of the park. I loved Rip Torn in this as well. Shitty shitty shitty CGI. The practical effects in this were awwwwwwesome but the digital shit? Lost in Space grade. Even the CGI mouth on the pug looked like ass. If only they'd known how TERRIBLY it would age. Alas... Was this movie a little racist? Barry Sonnenfeld, nothing on God's Green Earth can make me forgive you for Nine Lives. MiB, though, is a welcomed part of our healing process. Five Mutzies and Glicks
